summary: Standards: tier_purge_preview_03 does not build the scenario's Given ('the same repository with the bucket variable set to a bucket the tier can attach'): it never declares the cold tier, so it proves 'a repository with no unattached tier offers the commit' (0.39 behavior) and not the blocked-to-attachable transition. The debug seam CANON_R2_LOCAL_ROOT (+ CANON_R2_BUCKET set) attaches a cold s3 tier in a test. I ran the real binary with a declared cold tier: unset -> unavailable names cold and no --commit step; with CANON_R2_BUCKET and CANON_R2_LOCAL_ROOT set -> unavailable [] and meta.next[0] is the --commit command, and that commit deleted the old git-tier session row (kept the new one). So the behavior holds; the test is the weak part. Blast radius: a regression that blocked previews for every repo declaring a cold tier would not fail this test.
